claims.nodeLabel: Area 51 (Homey Airport / Groom Lake operating location)
claims.sourceText: The Lazar Tape, Tri-Dot Productions, 1991, captions at 2:07, https://archive.org/details/antigravity ; and Las Vegas Review-Journal, 19 June 1990, p 8B, opened 2026-09-18
claims.text: The 1989 KLAS-TV Lazar broadcasts are the single event most responsible for this place entering worldwide public consciousness under this name. Lazar's own 1991 narration refers to 'the infamous Area 51 installation at Groom Lake' and places his claimed S-4 site about fifteen miles south of it. A contemporaneous newspaper of 19 June 1990 confirms the broadcasts existed and that Lazar was their focal point.

claims.sourceText: The Lazar Tape, Tri-Dot Productions, 1991, captions at 35:48 to 36:32 via YouTube video kc10m6HFbDE, https://archive.org/details/antigravity , opened 2026-09-18
claims.text: Bob Lazar claims Teller as his route into the classified work, in his own 1991 narration: 'while working at Los Alamos National Lab in 1982 the local newspaper did a front page story on a jet car [I'd] built coincidentally Dr Teller was giving a speech in Los Alamos that same day we met and had a short chat'. He says he later wrote to Teller and 'inquired about a job', and that 'Dr Teller responded by telephone and told me that it was no longer active but' referred him on. He adds that he never asked Teller whether he remembered him. The claim is uncorroborated by any opened record and its internal dating conflicts with the newspaper's own date of 27 June 1982, Teller's Los Alamos lecture falling on the following day per Mahood. Carried at Tier 3 and asserting only what Lazar said.

claims.nodeLabel: Element 115: the Lazar claim and moscovium
claims.sourceText: The Lazar Tape, Tri-Dot Productions, 1991, captions at 10:43 and 14:14 to 14:26, https://archive.org/details/antigravity , opened 2026-09-18
claims.text: THE LOAD-BEARING PHYSICAL CLAIM, which is the one the physics objections attack: 'The most important attribute of these heavier stable elements is that the gravity a wave is so abundant that it actually extends past the perimeter of the atom', and separately 'gravity a is what is currently being labeled as the strong nuclear force in mainstream physics'.

claims.nodeLabel: Element 115: the Lazar claim and moscovium
claims.sourceText: The Lazar Tape and Excerpts from the Government Bible, Tri-Dot Productions, 1991, captions via YouTube video kc10m6HFbDE, https://archive.org/details/antigravity , opened 2026-09-18
claims.text: WHAT LAZAR CLAIMED, in his own 1991 narration. That stable superheavy elements exist 'in the 114 115 range which don't appear on a periodic chart' and that 'Beyond Element 115 the elements become unstable again and in fact element 116 decays in fractions of a second'. That 'the power source is a reactor which uses this element 115 as its fuel', with 115 'used as a Target and is bombarded with protons', a proton entering a 115 nucleus producing 'an atom of element 116 which remember decays instantly', radiating antimatter which is then annihilated for power. That 'only 223 grams of 115 which is just under half a pound can be utilized for a period of 20 to 30 years', that 'element 115's melting point is 1740 degrees Celsius', and that 'the element 115 is machined into triangles like this and is then inserted into the reactor'. Auto-generated captions at 18:42, 19:01, 23:31 and 25:34, so wording is approximate.

claims.sourceText: The Lazar tape and excerpts from the Government Bible, Internet Archive item, creator Gene Huff and Bob Lazar, publisher Tri-Dot Productions, 1991, https://archive.org/details/antigravity , opened 2026-09-18
claims.text: He wrote and co-produced the 1991 videotape The Lazar Tape and Excerpts from the Government Bible for Tri-Dot Productions, credited alongside Bob Lazar. This makes him the publisher of the primary artefact of the entire cluster.

claims.sourceText: The Lazar Tape, Tri-Dot Productions, 1991, captions at 2:07 and 27:16 via YouTube video kc10m6HFbDE, https://archive.org/details/antigravity , opened 2026-09-18
claims.text: Bob Lazar's 1991 narration sites his claimed S-4 facility by reference to this place, 'approximately 15 miles south of the infamous Area 51 installation at Groom Lake', and says he was bussed from there to the claimed site. The claim is anchored geographically to a documented facility; that anchoring does not transfer the facility's documentation to the claim.

claims.nodeLabel: Nellis Air Force Base and the Nevada Test and Training Range
claims.sourceText: The Lazar Tape, Tri-Dot Productions, 1991, captions at 2:02 via YouTube video kc10m6HFbDE, https://archive.org/details/antigravity , opened 2026-09-18
claims.text: Bob Lazar places his claimed S-4 facility on this range: 'a facility at an area known as S4 on the Nellis Air Force range in central Nevada'. No government record naming any such facility on the range was opened by this board.

claims.sourceText: Stanton T. Friedman, 'The Bob Lazar Fraud', https://www.theblackvault.com/casefiles/the-bob-lazar-fraud-2/ ; and The Lazar Tape, 1991, captions at 2:19, https://archive.org/details/antigravity , both opened 2026-09-18
claims.text: A DISCREPANCY, NOT A RELATIONSHIP. The W-2 form in the Lazar literature is described as naming a 'Department of Naval Intelligence', which is not an entity that exists: the Office of Naval Intelligence sits inside the Department of the Navy. Stanton Friedman, who had seen the form, describes it only as 'His W-2 form from the Department of Naval Intelligence totals under $1000.00, at most a week's pay for a scientist.' Lazar's own 1991 narration says something different again: 'for the duration of my employment at S4 I was paid by the United States Navy'. THE FORM ITSELF WAS NOT OPENED BY THIS BOARD AND NO EMPLOYER IDENTIFICATION NUMBER, ZIP CODE OR BOX CONTENT IS ASSERTED ANYWHERE.

claims.locator: YouTube video kc10m6HFbDE at 1:41, 1:54, 2:19, 24:24 and 28:01, opened 2026-09-18
claims.sourceText: The Lazar Tape and Excerpts from the Government Bible, Tri-Dot Productions, 1991, captions read via YouTube video kc10m6HFbDE at 1:41, 1:54, 2:19, 24:24 and 28:01, opened 2026-09-18
claims.text: In his own narration on the 1991 videotape he states the shape of the claim: that he held 'secret and Above Top Secret security clearances of which the most easily verifiable is my early 1980s job here at the Los Alamos Ma[e]son physics facility'; that 'between December of 88 and April of 89' he worked at 'a facility at an area known as S4 on the Nellis Air Force range in central Nevada', 'approximately 15 miles south of the infamous Area 51 installation at Groom Lake'; that 'for the duration of my employment at S4 I was paid by the United States Navy'; that 'the S4 installation is built into the mountain and the nine Hangar doors are angled at about 60 degrees'; and that he had 'at least partial views of nine different discs out at area S4'. Auto-generated captions, so wording is approximate.

claims.text: THE CLAIM, in the claimant's own narration on the 1991 videotape: 'between December of 88 and April of 89' he worked at 'a facility at an area known as S4 on the Nellis Air Force range in central Nevada', 'approximately 15 miles south of the infamous Area 51 installation at Groom Lake'; 'The S4 installation is built into the mountain and the nine Hangar doors are angled at about 60 degrees'; he was bussed there from near 'the gro[o]m mountains in the groom[ ]dry lake bed from Area 51... to an even more highly secure' site; and he had 'at least partial views of nine different discs out at area S4'.
